please implement a feature that allows any visitor to type something within reason like maybe about 500 characters or something 
and then any visitor to the website will instantly see this text as well 
there is no persistence and no guarantee of up time 
so we should probably get rid of any older messages as newer messages come in 
overall the website should be resilient and roll with the punches 
there is no need to support anything but the latest evergreen browser versions 
so please keep the html and css as clean as possible with this in mind 
also somewhere either the header or the footer it should show the current server time and it should keep ticking once a second 
it is critical for the website to be fully responsive 
yes, only evergreen browsers but should work fine on android, iPhone, as well as the desktop / laptop browsers

How it works

Message board: a singleton holds the newest 50 messages in memory. Older ones drop off as new ones arrive. Each post replaces an immutable array, then notifies subscribers. A subscriber that throws gets logged and skipped, so one bad subscriber can't break the others.
Input handling: messages are capped at 500 characters on the client (maxlength) and enforced again on the server. The server also strips control characters, collapses runs of blank lines, avoids cutting a surrogate pair in half, and rejects posts that are only whitespace or invisible characters. Each visitor has a 2-second cooldown between posts.
Clock: one background timer for the whole server, aligned to each second. Every connected page subscribes to it, so there isn't one timer per visitor. It appears in the header and uses tabular numbers so the digits don't jitter.
Before the page goes live: both components subscribe only once the page is interactive (RendererInfo.IsInteractive). The send button stays disabled until then. The first render already shows the current messages and time.
Memory and reconnects: disconnected sessions are kept for 1 minute, at most 20 of them, which suits the 256 MB cap. After a restart, the built-in Blazor reconnect reloads the page by itself once the server answers.
CSS: colours come from light-dark() tokens, which replace the old media queries. There's no fixed width anywhere, the header wraps on narrow screens, long text wraps, and the textarea's 16px font prevents iOS from zooming in. I removed the unused form-validation and error-boundary styles.
This container has no .NET SDK, so I couldn't build it here. Run dotnet build before you push.
